title: OpenAI Chat Completions wire symmetrizer and response fidelity guard
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: Implement a compatibility layer that converts between Redwood's internal chat event model and the OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request/response wire format while preserving streaming fidelity, function/tool-call semantics, structured output envelopes, and message provenance.

Scope:
- Request-side: map Redwood chat/message model -> OpenAI request payloads (messages, system/user/assistant roles, function schemas) with a pluggable sanitizer and idempotency token.
- Response-side: ingest OpenAI streaming chunk/event sequences and reconstruct Redwood streaming frames, ensuring structured JSON objects are validated and tool/function calls are emitted as first-class events.
- Maintain backwards-compatibility for legacy clients relying on OpenAI-styled SSE framing.
- Emit telemetry and per-token latency/cost signals for Console traceability.

Out of scope: model-side behavioral adjustments (prompt engineering), Dedicated autoscaling changes, private deployment-only networking plumbing.
acceptance_criteria: Requests generated by the symmetrizer from Redwood chat objects produce semantically equivalent OpenAI ChatCompletions payloads in unit tests (>= 95% coverage for mapped fields)
Streaming responses from OpenAI-like providers are reconstituted into Redwood stream frames with preserved chunk ordering, function call start/finish boundaries, and incremental content deltas
Function/tool call events are emitted exactly once with complete arguments parsed into Redwood ToolCall schema and an idempotency token attached
Structured-output objects embedded in assistant messages are validated against provided JSON schemas; invalid payloads produce a structured error event without dropping the entire stream
Telemetry includes: first-byte latency, per-chunk token counts, tool invocation counts, and a compact provenance header that traces original request id -> provider request id -> response id
Compatibility mode can be toggled (strict-openai | permissive-redwood) without server restart and is exercised by integration tests
No regression in existing Redwood streaming tests (compare baseline traces) and load tests show <5% tail latency increase for 95th percentile compared to current proxy
tasks: Draft request and response mapping tables (fields, transforms, default fallbacks)
Implement OpenAI wire marshaller for requests with sanitizer hooks for user metadata and function schema injection
Build stream reassembler that consumes provider SSE/chunk stream and emits Redwood streaming frames including tool-call boundaries
Add JSON schema validator for structured-output blocks and error-envelope emitter
Instrument telemetry hooks in marshaller and reassembler (tracing ids, token counters)
Create unit and integration tests including recorded golden streams and a local fake provider for edge cases
Prepare migration notes and console dashboard tiles for new provenance fields

2026-03-11 - Rajesh Kulkarni (Runtime): Code review feedback: ensure backpressure signals from Redwood runtime are propagated to provider stream consumer to avoid unbounded buffering. Added to tasks.

2026-03-12 - QA: Found flaky test where tool-call finalization event was lost when provider sends termination without explicit finish token. Added test and mitigation strategy: finalize on stream close if open tool-call present.
notes: Design trade-offs: we prefer preserving provider chunk boundaries where possible to give clients identical streaming shape, but for safety we coalesce small JSON fragments to ensure valid structured blocks.
Performance consideration: per-stream reassembly buffer is configurable; default 64KB with fallback to fallthrough mode that emits raw chunks plus a warning when exceeded.
Rollout plan: feature flag behind 'oa-wire-symmetrizer'; start with 5% of hosted traffic, monitor tool-call correctness metric and 95th latency for 48h, then ramp.
Fallback behavior: on provider schema parsing error, emit structured ERROR event with raw payload link and continue streaming if possible.
